strengths: T2 Systems Thinker rejects the simple-pipe view and introduces ocean-atmosphere feedback.
T4 Physical Geographer concedes prevailing winds shape the currents, narrowing T1's claim.
T9 stage-and-lighting metaphor and Section E's AMOC pointer give memorable, concrete handles.
weaknesses: T1-T9 never raise westerly winds, maritime versus continental coasts, or mountain-driven air flow.
Historical Contextualist turns T3, T6, T9 recast the explanation as human history.
Section D folds human adaptation into the cause; T7 agreement has no stated cause.

findings.description: Synthesis lists historical human adaptation as part of the temperature difference; T3 itself treats human history as a result of the warmth, so the synthesis contradicts the debate's own causal direction.

Ocean currents are presented as the primary driver; climate literature gives large weight to atmospheric heat transport by westerlies onto a western coast versus continental air on eastern Canada, which the debate omits.
The North Atlantic current is described as a stock maintained by density differences; the surface current is largely wind-driven and is a flow, conflating it with the overturning circulation.
Quoted Humboldt sentence may not match the wording of any English translation of Cosmos; no translation is named.
European warmth called a temporary geological favor without support or timescale.
Braudel's The Mediterranean concerns the Mediterranean world; claims about Europe versus the Canadian north are not drawn from that book.

rubric_fit_notes: For a physical-science why-question, criterion 4 has little natural room; it was scored on whether the common warm-current assumption was examined, not on absent life motives. The cap entry rests on the synthesis contradicting the debate's own T3 causal direction; the omission of atmospheric explanations is held as suspected only.
question_type_note: Read as exploratory: criteria 4 and 5 judged on examining the user's assumptions and defining and deciding between competing physical explanations, with no deduction for missing a life decision.
